# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

1 | # ⚡ PowerGrid AI — Predictive Outage & Equipment Failure Advisor
2 | 
3 | > **Predict. Prevent. Keep the Grid On.**  
4 | > An AI-powered decision-support platform for modern electrical grids that predicts equipment failures, estimates customer outage impacts, maps high-voltage transmission networks, and automates field crew dispatch before an outage occurs.
5 | 
6 | ---
7 | 
8 | ## 🌟 Key Features
9 | 
10 | - **🗺️ Interactive Gujarat Grid Map (836+ Assets across all 33 Districts):**
11 |   - **12 Real Power Generation Stations:** Mundra Thermal (4,620 MW), Khavda Hybrid Solar/Wind (30,000 MW), Kakrapar Nuclear (1,400 MW), Charanka Solar (600 MW), Ukai Hydro, Gandhinagar GSECL, Wanakbori, Sardar Sarovar, etc.
12 |   - **GETCO High-Voltage Substations & Distribution Transformers** mapped to authentic GPS coordinates with animated 400kV/220kV transmission line corridors.
13 |   - **MapTiler Layer Switcher:** Toggle between **🌑 Dark SCADA**, **🛰️ Satellite Aerial**, and **🗺️ Highway Grid** views.
14 |   - **Real-Time Visual Indicators:** Pulsing red radar circles on Critical risk nodes, tilted diamond badges for substations, and hexagonal badges for power generation stations.
15 | 
16 | - **🤖 Machine Learning Failure Engine (XGBoost):**
17 |   - Trained on Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) chemistry ($C_2H_2, C_2H_4, CH_4, H_2, CO, CO_2$), IEC 60599 Rogers Ratios, dielectric oil rigidity, winding temperatures, and operational vibration/load.
18 |   - **96.25% Multi-Class Fault Classification Accuracy:** Diagnoses *Arcing / Partial Discharge*, *Thermal Overheating*, *Insulation Degradation*, *Dielectric Breakdown*, and *Mechanical Strain*.
19 |   - **Failure Probability & Health Index Scoring (0–100):** Predicts risk horizon windows (`6h`, `24h`, `48h`, `7d`).
20 | 
21 | - **🧪 Interactive AI Testing Studio (For Judges & Operators):**
22 |   - Live sensor sliders to input or simulate arbitrary operational telemetry on the fly.
23 |   - 4 instant one-click demonstration presets:
24 |     1. *Normal Safe Operation* ($48^\circ\text{C}$, low gas)
25 |     2. *Critical Arcing & Breakdown* ($C_2H_2 = 38\text{ ppm}$, partial discharge)
26 |     3. *Severe Thermal Overheating* ($98^\circ\text{C}$ oil temp, $118\%$ load)
27 |     4. *High Vibration Mechanical Strain* ($6.8\text{ mm/s}$)
28 |   - Real-time inference output with SHAP feature importance attribution and automated crew dispatch recommendations.
29 | 
30 | - **👥 Automated Field Crew Dispatch:**
31 |   - 12 Gujarat field crews across 6 operational zones (Ahmedabad North/South, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, Gandhinagar) with skill-level tracking (Substation Engineers, Senior Linemen, Specialists).

77 | def calculate_grid_impact(asset: Asset) -> float:
78 |     """
79 |     Grid Impact Severity Model accounting for:
80 |       - Number of customers served
81 |       - Presence of critical facilities (hospitals, water works, emergency responders)
82 |       - Voltage class (kV)
83 |       - MVA capacity
84 |     Returns normalized 0-100 score.
85 |     """
86 |     customers = asset.customers_served or 15000
87 |     facilities = asset.critical_facilities or 2
88 |     voltage = asset.voltage_kv or 66.0
89 |     capacity = asset.capacity_mva or 40.0
90 | 
91 |     # Logarithmic population scaling (matches CPI formula in dashboard.py)
92 |     # log10(max(100, C)) / 5.301  → saturates at ~200k customers = 1.0
93 |     cust_norm = min(1.0, math.log10(max(100, customers)) / 5.301)
94 |     fac_norm = min(1.0, facilities / 8.0)
95 |     volt_norm = min(1.0, voltage / 400.0)
96 |     cap_norm = min(1.0, capacity / 120.0)
97 | 
98 |     # 35% customers (log-scaled) + 25% critical facilities + 25% voltage class + 15% capacity
99 |     score = (0.35 * cust_norm + 0.25 * fac_norm + 0.25 * volt_norm + 0.15 * cap_norm) * 100.0
100 |     return round(score, 1)

103 | def haversine_km(lat1: float, lon1: float, lat2: float, lon2: float) -> float:
104 |     """Compute great circle distance in km between two geo coordinates."""
105 |     r = 6371.0
106 |     dlat = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)
107 |     dlon = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)
108 |     a = math.sin(dlat / 2.0) ** 2 + math.cos(math.radians(lat1)) * math.cos(math.radians(lat2)) * math.sin(dlon / 2.0) ** 2
109 |     c = 2.0 * math.atan2(math.sqrt(a), math.sqrt(1.0 - a))
110 |     return r * c

arguments.description: Full code audit covering security, logic, ML, API, and frontend issues found across the ThreatOps PowerGrid AI codebase.
arguments.html:
ThreatOps — Code Loophole Audit

PowerGrid AI · Gujarat SCADA Platform · Full static analysis across backend (Python/FastAPI) and frontend (Next.js/TypeScript)

3
Critical
6
High
7
Medium
4
Low / Info
20
Total Issues

🔴 Critical

CRITICAL
Security · Credential Exposure
Live database credentials and MapTiler API key committed to version control
backend/app/db/database.py · backend/.env.example · frontend/src/components/GridMap.tsx

database.py line 13 hardcodes the full Neon PostgreSQL connection string (including plaintext password npg_rFvRn3LNpm0q) as the default fallback. .env.example also contains the real live credentials rather than placeholder values. The MapTiler key CRFoY3RXgAloQLarTcRL is hardcoded directly in GridMap.tsx line 6 and in .env.example.

Anyone who clones the repository has immediate read/write access to the production Neon database and can exhaust the MapTiler quota.

Fix Remove all real credentials from both files. The database.py fallback should raise a clear RuntimeError("DATABASE_URL env var not set") if missing. Replace .env.example values with your-password-here placeholders. Pass the MapTiler key via an environment variable (NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPTILER_KEY) and read it at runtime.
CRITICAL
Security · API
No authentication or authorisation on any API endpoint
backend/app/main.py · all routers

Every endpoint — including POST /api/planning/work-orders, POST /api/planning/work-orders/{wo_id}/verify-interlock, POST /api/predictions/batch-audit, and POST /api/predictions/predict — is completely unauthenticated. Any client on the network can create work orders, verify SCADA interlocks, or run arbitrary ML inference against the live production database. The only protection is the CORS origin whitelist, which only applies to browser clients and provides no protection against direct API calls (curl, Postman, scripts).

Fix Add an API-key or JWT dependency on at minimum all POST/mutating endpoints. FastAPI makes this trivial with an HTTPBearer or APIKeyHeader security dependency injected via Depends().
CRITICAL
ML · Reproducibility
Training script uses absolute local Windows paths — model cannot be retrained on any other machine
backend/app/ml/train.py · lines 24–25

Lines 24–25 hardcode DGA_ZIP = r"C:\Users\Manthan\Downloads\faulty dataset with prediction.zip" and FAULT_ZIP = r"C:\Users\Manthan\Downloads\faulty data-set.zip". Any collaborator running python -m app.ml.train falls silently into the synthetic-data-only path because the ZIP files are missing — but there is no warning about the path mismatch specifically, and the printed warning only says "DGA ZIP not found". The trained model accuracy would differ significantly from the 96.25% claimed value. This also means the FAULT_ZIP is referenced but never actually opened anywhere in the function.

Fix Replace hardcoded paths with a configurable path: read from an env var or accept a CLI argument. Add the dataset files to a data/ directory (or document download instructions). Also wire up the unused FAULT_ZIP or remove the variable.

🟠 High

HIGH
Security · CORS
CORS allows all methods and all headers — overly permissive
backend/app/main.py · lines 12–18

allow_methods=["*"] and allow_headers=["*"] permit any method (including DELETE, PATCH, PUT) and any custom header from the frontend origin. Since there are no DELETE/PATCH endpoints today this is harmless, but it sets a permissive baseline that will silently allow future mutating routes from the browser without any additional configuration.

Fix Restrict to the methods actually in use: allow_methods=["GET", "POST"] and enumerate only the needed headers, e.g. allow_headers=["Content-Type", "Authorization"].
HIGH
API · Input Validation
No upper-bound limit on limit query parameter — allows unbounded DB scans
backend/app/api/risks.py · assets.py · incidents.py · planning.py

GET /api/risks/?limit=999999, GET /api/assets/?limit=999999, and GET /api/incidents/?limit=999999 all accept any integer without a cap. The frontend even calls fetchAssets(1000). On a table with 836+ assets and growing sensor/incident rows, a runaway limit can produce a very large result set and time out the Neon serverless connection pool.

Fix Add Query(default, ge=1, le=500) validation (matching the existing pattern already used in sensors.py's hours parameter). Cap the /api/assets frontend call at a reasonable page size and implement cursor/offset pagination.
HIGH
API · Input Validation
Unvalidated free-text district and asset_id filter parameters
backend/app/api/assets.py · incidents.py · planning.py

In assets.py the district filter uses Asset.district == district (exact match via SQLAlchemy ORM — safe from SQL injection but case-sensitive and undocumented). In planning.py line 185 it uses .ilike(f"%{district}%") which is a wildcard search and would match partial strings. No length or character-set validation is applied to either parameter. A value like district=A%A%A%A%A%A%A%A%A% creates a pathological LIKE pattern in PostgreSQL.

Fix Add Query(None, max_length=100, regex="^[a-zA-Z0-9 \\-]*$") on district and similar string filters. Avoid unbounded ILIKE wildcards on user input.
HIGH
ML · Data Leakage
Model trained and evaluated on data generated by the same deterministic formula — inflated accuracy
backend/app/ml/train.py · lines 105–124

The ground-truth label failure_probability and fault_mode are computed from the same feature values using a fixed formula (lines 105–124), then the model is trained to reproduce that formula. The reported 96.25% accuracy and R²=0.60 are measured against held-out samples drawn from the same generative distribution. This is circular evaluation — the model learns the formula, not real failure physics. When the DGA ZIP is absent (the common case after cloning), 100% of the training set is synthetic, making the classifier a function approximator of a hand-coded rule rather than an ML model.

Fix Clearly document that the model's accuracy metrics apply only to the synthetic distribution. Evaluate on a truly held-out real-world DGA dataset. Add a metadata field "training_data": "synthetic" vs "real_dga" so the API's /model-info response is honest.
HIGH
Logic · ML Service
Post-hoc probability calibration overrides model output — silent business logic manipulation
backend/app/services/ml_service.py · lines 133–147

After the XGBoost regressor produces raw_prob, up to +0.35 (arcing), +0.25 (temperature), +0.20 (vibration), and +0.20 (overload) escalation adjustments are added, and up to −0.22 relief is subtracted, before the final prob is returned. This means the model can be overridden by as much as ±1.0 of its actual output. The calibration is undocumented in the API response — callers receive a probability that has been silently modified without any indication of which path was taken.

Fix Return both raw_model_probability and calibrated_probability in the response, along with the applied adjustments. This makes the calibration transparent and auditable by operators.
HIGH
Frontend · State Integrity
Work orders and crew dispatch state exist only in React memory — lost on page refresh
frontend/src/app/page.tsx · lines 165, 523–542, 549–567

INITIAL_WORK_ORDERS is a hardcoded constant pre-populated with fake IDs like WO-2026-104. New work orders created via handleCreateWorkOrder() and dispatches via handleConfirmDispatch() only update React state — they are never persisted to the backend even though persistWorkOrder() exists in api.ts. Refreshing the page resets to the hardcoded list. Crew availability changes (line 524) similarly disappear on refresh.

Fix Call persistWorkOrder() inside handleCreateWorkOrder() and handleConfirmDispatch(), then refresh the list from the backend. Fetch the initial work orders from GET /api/planning/work-orders instead of using the hardcoded constant.

🟡 Medium

MEDIUM
Logic · DB Session
get_db() uses finally without rollback on exception — partial commits possible
backend/app/db/database.py · lines 19–24

The session generator closes the session in finally but never calls db.rollback() in an except branch. SQLAlchemy sessions with autocommit=False retain uncommitted state; if a route handler partially commits data and then raises an exception the session is closed in a dirty state. The standard FastAPI pattern wraps in a try/except/finally with explicit rollback.

Fix Add try: yield db / except: db.rollback(); raise / finally: db.close() to the generator.
MEDIUM
API · Error Handling
Several read endpoints return empty objects/lists instead of 404 on missing resources
backend/app/api/sensors.py · assets.py · predictions.py

GET /api/sensors/{asset_id}/history returns [] for an unknown asset (line 20). GET /api/sensors/{asset_id}/latest returns {} (line 80). GET /api/predictions/{asset_id} returns {} or the empty Prediction ORM object (line 215). The frontend cannot distinguish "asset does not exist" from "asset exists but has no data", making error display impossible.

Fix Raise HTTPException(status_code=404) when the asset row is not found. Return 404 vs 200 [] so callers can react correctly.
MEDIUM
Logic · ML Service
Models loaded once globally at process startup with no reload mechanism
backend/app/services/ml_service.py · lines 21–34

The module-level _regressor, _classifier, and _metadata singletons are never invalidated. If python -m app.ml.train is run to retrain the models, the running server process continues serving predictions from the stale in-memory models until the process is restarted. There is no way to hot-reload without a full server restart.

Fix Add a POST /api/predictions/reload-models admin endpoint (guarded by auth) that calls a new reload_models() function which sets _regressor = None and re-calls load_models(). Or use a FastAPI lifespan event to load once at startup with a proper singleton.
MEDIUM
Logic · Planning
Crew pre-positioning crashes with ZeroDivisionError if no assignments are returned
backend/app/api/planning.py · line 509

Line 509 computes avg_savings = round(sum(...) / len(prepositioning_assignments), 1). If prepositioning_assignments is empty (e.g. the Hungarian solver returns no matches because crews is empty after a DB state inconsistency), this raises an unhandled ZeroDivisionError that becomes an unformatted 500 error. The early-return guard at line 361 only checks for zero crews fetched from the DB — it does not guard the post-solver list.

Fix Guard with avg_savings = round(...) if prepositioning_assignments else 0.0.
MEDIUM
Logic · API
GET /api/assets/critical and GET /api/assets/{asset_id} route ordering conflict
backend/app/api/assets.py · lines 50–73

FastAPI resolves routes in registration order. /critical is defined before /{asset_id}, so it works today. However this is fragile — if the order is ever reversed (e.g. during a refactor), the string "critical" will be matched as an asset_id path parameter, returning a 404 instead of the critical assets list. Similarly, GET /api/predictions/, /model-info, /live/{asset_id}, and /{asset_id} share the same router with no explicit ordering documentation.

Fix Use a distinct prefix for special sub-routes (e.g. /meta/critical) or add a comment that the literal routes must always precede parameterized ones in this file.
MEDIUM
Frontend · Race Condition
Auto-stream interval calls handleSimulate() with stale closure state
frontend/src/app/page.tsx · lines 449–483

The setInterval callback at line 452 calls handleSimulate() with no argument (line 479), which reads simTemp, simVibration, etc. from the closure. Because React state updates are asynchronous and the set* calls inside the interval happen before the re-render, handleSimulate() reads the previous state values rather than the just-updated ones, sending stale telemetry to the inference API every 2.5 seconds.

Fix Use a useRef to track the latest sensor values (updated in each setter), or restructure the effect to collect final values before calling handleSimulate, passing them as an explicit customPayload.
MEDIUM
ML · Logic
FAULT_ZIP variable is defined but never used — dead code
backend/app/ml/train.py · line 25

FAULT_ZIP is defined on line 25 and referenced nowhere in load_and_prepare_dataset(). Only the DGA ZIP is conditionally opened. The fault dataset is either silently skipped or the author intended to use it for a second data source that was never implemented.

Fix Either implement loading from FAULT_ZIP to supplement the dataset, or remove the variable and update the docstring so it doesn't claim two ZIPs are used.

🟢 Low / Informational

LOW
Code Quality
clean_f / clean_float helper is duplicated in 4 separate files
backend/app/api/sensors.py · weather.py (2× in sensors.py, 1× in weather.py)

The clean_f/clean_float function (strip NaN/Inf, return default) is copy-pasted across sensors.py (three times — once per endpoint, all identical) and weather.py. Any bug fix needs to be applied in multiple places.

Fix Extract to a shared utility module, e.g. app/utils.py, and import where needed.
LOW
Code Quality · Python
import math placed inside function bodies instead of at module level
backend/app/api/sensors.py · weather.py · planning.py

Multiple files call import math, import json, from sqlalchemy import func inside individual route handler functions rather than at module top level. Python caches imports so there is no correctness issue, but it is non-idiomatic, hides the module's true dependencies from static analysis tools, and makes the imports impossible to mock in unit tests.

Fix Move all imports to the top of each file.
LOW
Performance · DB
N+1 query in get_prioritised_maintenance_plan — one query per asset in loop
backend/app/api/planning.py · lines 233–240

Inside the results loop, lines 233–236 issue a SELECT … ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1 for the latest sensor reading of each asset, and lines 239–240 issue a SELECT COUNT(*) for incidents. For 50 work orders this is 100 additional queries per request to the Neon serverless pool.

Fix Use a single query with a subquery (like the pattern in predictions.py's batch-audit route) to fetch all latest sensor readings in one round trip before the loop.
LOW
Requirements · Dependency
scipy used in production but missing from requirements.txt
backend/requirements.txt · backend/app/api/planning.py line 23

from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment is imported in planning.py, but scipy does not appear in requirements.txt. Fresh installs will fail at runtime when the /api/planning/crew-prepositioning endpoint is hit. The venv happens to have scipy installed (scipy-1.18.1) but a clean pip install -r requirements.txt will not install it.

Fix Add scipy>=1.11.0 to requirements.txt.

ML / Model Integrity4Critical
API Input Validation3High
Logic / Runtime Errors4High

Found **20 issues** across the full stack. Here's the executive summary:

---

### 🔴 Critical (3)

1. **Live DB credentials & MapTiler API key committed to git** — [`database.py:13`](backend/app/db/database.py:13) and [`GridMap.tsx:6`](frontend/src/components/GridMap.tsx:6) contain real plaintext passwords. Anyone cloning the repo has full DB access.

2. **Zero authentication on all API endpoints** — every `POST` route including `verify-interlock` and `batch-audit` is fully public. CORS only blocks browsers, not direct API calls.

3. **Hardcoded absolute `C:\Users\Manthan\Downloads\...` paths in [`train.py`](backend/app/ml/train.py:24)** — model can never be retrained by anyone else; falls silently to synthetic-only data. `FAULT_ZIP` is defined but never opened anywhere.

---

### 🟠 High (6)

4. **CORS allows all methods + all headers** — unnecessarily permissive baseline in [`main.py`](backend/app/main.py:13).
5. **No upper bound on `limit` query param** — `GET /api/assets/?limit=999999` causes unbounded DB scans across multiple routers.
6. **Unvalidated string filter params** — wildcard `ILIKE "%value%"` in [`planning.py:185`](backend/app/api/planning.py:185) is vulnerable to pathological patterns.
7. **Inflated 96.25% accuracy is circular** — model is trained and evaluated on data generated by the same formula it learns. It's approximating a hardcoded rule, not real physics.
8. **Silent post-hoc probability manipulation** — ML service overrides model output by up to ±1.0 via undisclosed calibration; callers see a modified number with no transparency.
9. **Work orders & crew dispatch only exist in React state** — lost on page refresh; `persistWorkOrder()` in [`api.ts`](frontend/src/lib/api.ts:117) exists but is never called from the UI handlers.

---

### 🟡 Medium (7) · 🟢 Low (4)

Including: missing `rollback` in the DB session generator, endpoints returning `{}` instead of 404, stale-closure race condition in the auto-stream interval, `ZeroDivisionError` if the Hungarian solver returns empty assignments, route ordering fragility (`/critical` vs `/{asset_id}`), `clean_f` helper duplicated 4 times across files, and **`scipy` missing from `requirements.txt`** despite being a production import.
